title: Metaphysics of science and physics seminar
stage: Graduate study and research in metaphysics
audience: a philosophy graduate preparing for doctoral study and research in metaphysics, or a graduate student in the first years of a PhD
purpose: Study current research where metaphysics meets physics: naturalized metaphysics, the metaphysics of spacetime (substantivalism, relationalism and the hole argument), laws, symmetries and structure, chance, the direction of time and the past hypothesis, the metaphysics of quantum mechanics (wave function realism, primitive ontology, many worlds and branching), nonlocality and relativity, emergence, and the possible emergence of spacetime in quantum gravity.
primary_reading: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy: Quantum Mechanics (free)

weeks.2: The metaphysics of spacetime: substantivalism and relationalism
weeks.3: The hole argument and its responses
weeks.6: The direction of time and the past hypothesis
weeks.7: Wave function realism and primitive ontology
weeks.11: Quantum gravity and the possible emergence of spacetime
weeks.12: Writing and presenting a seminar paper

blocks.deliverable: Write a response paper on naturalized metaphysics.
Explain how the past hypothesis is meant to ground the arrow of time.
Week 7 midterm; write a seminar paper proposal.
Present the tension between nonlocality and relativity.
Submit a seminar paper draft for review.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Seminar paper: write a 5,000- to 7,000-word seminar paper on one question at the boundary of metaphysics and physics (the hole argument, wave function realism, probability in many worlds or the past hypothesis) that presents the physics accurately, surveys the literature and defends an original thesis; revise it after written feedback.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
